_about: Answer key for the 18 MASVS benchmark questions (numbered 2-19 like the evaluation sheets). 'groups': each inner list is one topic; a topic counts as retrieved when any of its pages reached the model. 'expect': the facts a good answer states, taken from OWASP_MASVS.pdf v2.1.0. 'notInDoc': the document does not cover the topic, so the right answer says so.

2.expect: Mobile Application Security Verification Standard by OWASP; industry standard / baseline for mobile app security; set of controls; used as metric, guidance and baseline during development, testing and procurement.

3.expect: Eight control groups: STORAGE, CRYPTO, AUTH, NETWORK, PLATFORM, CODE, RESILIENCE, PRIVACY.

4.expect: STORAGE-1 app securely stores sensitive data; STORAGE-2 prevents leakage (backups, logs, public locations); covers PII, keys, secrets, API keys.

5.expect: Encrypted channel / TLS with endpoint authentication; NETWORK-1 secures all traffic per best practices; NETWORK-2 identity (certificate/public key) pinning; do not disable platform secure defaults.

6.expect: Devices are portable/lost/stolen; encryption protects sensitive data from physical access; use industry best practices (NIST); key management.

7.expect: AUTH-1 secure auth/authz protocols and best practices; AUTH-2 secure local authentication per platform best practices; AUTH-3 additional authentication (biometrics, PIN, MFA) for sensitive operations.

8.expect: Store sensitive data securely and prevent leakage (STORAGE-1/2); protect it with strong cryptography and proper key management (CRYPTO).

9.expect: Entry points (UI, IPC, network, file system) may carry data modified by untrusted actors; treat as untrusted, verify and sanitize; prevents SQL injection, XSS, insecure deserialization; CODE-4.

10.expect: The document does not discuss session management; at most relate to AUTH controls and say the topic is not covered.

11.expect: Unintentional exposure of PII, keys, secrets: stored in public locations, leaked via backups, logs, system/APIs; other apps or attackers can access it.

12.expect: Encrypt traffic (TLS), authenticate endpoint, NETWORK-1 secure all traffic, NETWORK-2 identity/certificate pinning.

13.expect: Baseline for privacy (not full GDPR/ENISA coverage); PRIVACY-1 minimize data/resources access; PRIVACY-2 prevent identification; PRIVACY-3 transparency about data collection; PRIVACY-4 user control over data.

14.expect: Increase resistance to reverse engineering and tampering to protect IP / business assets and against client-side attacks; platform integrity, anti-tampering, anti-static and anti-dynamic analysis; defense in depth, not a replacement for other controls.

15.expect: CRYPTO-2 key management per best practices across the lifecycle: generation, storage, protection; poor key management breaks strong crypto; NIST SP 800-57.

16.expect: Storage controls keep sensitive data in protected locations and prevent leaks; cryptography encrypts it so a lost/stolen device does not expose it; depends on proper key management.

17.expect: Authentication/authorization verify users and control access (protocols, local auth, extra factors); session management is not covered by the document and should be said so.

18.expect: TLS encryption + endpoint authentication protect confidentiality/integrity in transit; certificate validation and pinning (trusting only specific CAs) stop MITM; avoid bypassing platform defaults.

19.expect: Storage keeps data in safe locations and prevents leaks; cryptography encrypts it; privacy minimizes collected data, prevents identification and gives users transparency and control.
